title: The Blight - Folk Horror Music Pack, Plague Village and Witch Trial BGM - 44 Tracks
tagline: 44 track folk horror score: twelve village tunes heard warm, then wrong, and a bell from the first death on.
description:
The Blight is a 44 track folk horror music pack for games set in a plague village and a witch trial: 38 full looping pieces and 6 short cues, 61:14 of music, as OGG files with sample accurate loop tags plus all 44 editable MIDI sources. RPG Maker MV and MZ read the loop points with no plugin, and the Readme gives the import steps for Godot 4 (followed in a blank Godot 4.7.2 project, all 44 files), Unity and GameMaker. Royalty free for commercial games. Three full tracks are free to download on this page, with their MIDI.

One village, Thornwick, from May Day on the green to the ashes, in five acts. Act 1, Before the Blight: "Thornwick", "The Village Green", "Maying", "The Mill by the Water", "Market Day", "The Harvest", "The Wise Woman's Cottage", "Evensong", "The Green Man Inn", "Down by the River", "The Lovers' Walk" and "Midsummer Night". Act 2, The Sickness: "The First Death", "The Green Stands Empty", "The Plague Doctor", "The Mill Stands Still", "The Empty Inn", "The Shuttered Market", "The Harvest Rots", "Marked Doors", "The Dead Cart" and "The Church Doors Barred". Act 3, The Accusation: "Whispers", "The Witchfinder Arrives", "The Dance of the Dying", "The Mob", "The Cottage Is Watched", "The Woods at Night" and "Something in the Woods". Act 4, The Trial: "The Ducking", "The Gaol", "The Trial", "The Accused", "The Verdict", "The Pyre" and "The Hex". Act 5, Ashes: "Ashes on the Wind" and "Thornwick, After". Cues: "The Bell Tolls", "A Mark on the Door", "Witch!", "Guilty", "Spared" and "The Blight Spreads".

Warm, then wrong. Twelve tunes are heard twice. Before the blight each one is in a bright folk mode (ionian, mixolydian or dorian); after it, its twin plays the same tune on the same key note in a mode two or three steps darker (aeolian or phrygian), slower, on the same lead instrument over a new pad and a new bass, with the bell added. "The same tune" is literal: every lead note of every twin (1,354 notes) is the same scale degree as the warm tune's note, at the same tick, for the same length, read from the shipped MIDI, and the 491 notes that change pitch are the ones the darker mode lowers. Read against every other pair's tune instead of its own, every twin fails (132 of 132 readings). The pairs: "The Village Green" becomes "The Green Stands Empty"; "The Mill by the Water" becomes "The Mill Stands Still"; "The Green Man Inn" becomes "The Empty Inn"; "Market Day" becomes "The Shuttered Market"; "The Harvest" becomes "The Harvest Rots"; "Evensong" becomes "The Church Doors Barred"; "Maying" becomes "The Dance of the Dying"; "The Wise Woman's Cottage" becomes "The Cottage Is Watched"; "Down by the River" becomes "The Ducking"; "The Lovers' Walk" becomes "The Accused"; "Midsummer Night" becomes "The Pyre"; "Thornwick" becomes "Thornwick, After".

The passing bell. Tubular bells sound in none of the 12 tracks before the blight and in every one of the 32 tracks after it, 474 bell notes, from "The First Death" to the last cue. In a game, the first bell is the moment the village changes.

One theme. The seed, The May Song, leaps a fourth and walks home in three steps, and all 44 tracks state it in its own shape, counted by the harness in the finished MIDI. Five more cells come with it: The Hearth, four even quarters, for the mill, the market, the harvest and the inn; The River, for the wise woman's cottage, the river, the lovers and later the ducking stool; The Ember, for the May dance, the bonfire and later the pyre; The Toll, which opens on two half notes like a bell's two strokes, for the tracks of the sickness; and The Whisper, four quick eighths, for the tracks of the accusation. 2,151 statements and fragments of the 6 themes across the album.

Loops of a minute. Village and investigation scenes stay on one screen for a long time, so all 38 full pieces loop for at least a minute before they repeat: the shortest loop is 62.3 seconds, read from the LOOPLENGTH tag of the shipped OGG files. 8 of the faster pieces carry a third section to stay over the minute.

What is in it. 38 full pieces and 6 cues, 61:14 of music, 33 keys, 60 to 120 BPM, all in 4/4. 26 General MIDI instruments: whistle, recorder, ocarina, flute, oboe, English horn, bassoon, violin, viola, cello, contrabass, string ensemble, slow strings, tremolo strings, pizzicato strings, harp, nylon string guitar, harpsichord, dulcimer, choir aahs, voice oohs, reed organ, French horn, trombone, and as the only percussion timpani (1,007 notes) and tubular bells (474 notes). There is no drum kit and no synth. It is a score, not a sound design pack: every sound is a written note, with no noise beds and no processed drones.

What you get. 44 OGG files, 38 of them with sample accurate LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH tags, which is what RPG Maker MV and MZ read; each looping file ends exactly at its loop end. 44 editable .mid sources. A Readme with per engine import notes, the proof reports, and a royalty free commercial licence.

Gate results. 788 theory checks and 510 audio checks, 0 failed, and the reports ship inside the download. They say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks are for.

Three full tracks are free on this page, with their MIDI: "The Village Green" (ionian) and its twin "The Green Stands Empty" (aeolian, slower), so you can open both MIDI files and compare the leads note for note, and "The Hex", the final boss.

An honest note. The renders are a General MIDI reference render through a conventional soundfont, and the instruments are the General MIDI sounds of those names (a nylon string guitar plays where a lute would); the MIDI is there so you can use your own. No folk song, game, book or film cue is quoted; every tune was composed for this record. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used anywhere.

devlog.title: The Blight is out: a 44 track folk horror score where twelve village tunes come back wrong
devlog.body:
The Blight is a 44 track music pack for games set in a plague village and a witch trial: one village from May Day on the green through the sickness, the accusation and the trial to the ashes, plus six short cues. It is live now, with three full tracks free to download from the page.

The idea. Twelve tunes are heard twice. Before the blight each one is in a bright folk mode; after it, its twin plays the same tune, note for note, on the same key note in a mode two or three steps darker and slower (1,354 lead notes matched in the shipped MIDI, the 491 that change pitch being the ones the darker mode lowers). Tubular bells sound in none of the 12 tracks before the blight and in all 32 after it. The seed theme is stated in its own shape in all 44 tracks, and all 38 full pieces loop for a minute or more (shortest 62.3 seconds).

How it was checked. 788 theory checks and 510 audio checks, 0 failed, with the reports inside the download. The loop tags were followed into a blank Godot 4.7.2 project, all 44 files. Those numbers say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks ("The Village Green", "The Green Stands Empty" and "The Hex") are for: the first two are one pair.

The renders are a General MIDI reference render; the MIDI is there so you can move it to your own sounds. No folk song, game, book or film cue is quoted. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used.
